title: Cellar and Choir
premise: Petra Coldharbour, a hospice nurse who has spent twelve years hearing the dying count backwards, inherits Coldharbour House from a grandmother they never met — a house with a sealed cellar and a choir of voices that only sings when the frost comes. The sleep recordings reveal the truth: the founders bound something beneath the house, and it is fed by ritual every generation; Petra's bloodline is the lock. When the recordings capture a second voice answering questions — patient, hungry, learning Petra's name — they realize the binding is failing and the entity is reaching for them through love itself, wearing the faces of the found family Petra has built at the hospice. To survive, Petra must finish the founders' interrupted ritual before the first hard frost completes its pattern on the cellar glass, but doing so means choosing between duty to the dead who made them and love for the living who would die in their place. In the end Petra rewrites the ritual around consent instead of sacrifice, sealing the thing below not with a body but with a name freely given — their own — and walks out of the winter changed, half-anchored to the dark, no longer alone in either world.
about_author: E. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror from the quiet hours between rounds. They live somewhere cold, near water, and claim their house is perfectly ordinary.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. On the hospice night shift, Mrs. Adeyemi counts backwards from thirty and dies exactly at zero, as patients always do. Petra documents it calmly, professionally, refusing to call it anything but coincidence. The beat is controlled dread: we see how expertly Petra manages fear by naming it.

chapters.title: Letters from a Stranger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A solicitor's letter arrives: Grandmother Maren Coldharbour is dead, and Petra — disowned branch, twelve years estranged — inherits Coldharbour House outright. Petra's partner Dev finds the will's condition odd: Petra must winter there. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity wrestling with old family wounds.

chapters.title: The House That Waits
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. First arrival: frost on the inside of the windows, a cellar door nailed shut with brass nails arranged like sheet music. The neighbors cross the street rather than wave. Beat: unease sharpening into fascination — the house feels less abandoned than expectant.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Noises
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra catalogs the sounds: settling pipes, wind, something rhythmic beneath the floor that could be a boiler. Twelve years of practice making explanations. Dev calls nightly; Petra lies about how fine everything is. Beat: the reader sees the explanations straining.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, then a brief italicized interlude in an unknown voice. Petra pries one brass nail loose; the humming stops mid-note, offended. The unknown voice counts backwards from nine. Beat: first direct contact, small and terrible.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the attic, Petra finds Maren's ledger: generations of names, dates of first frost, dates of death — always within a week of each other. The last entry is Maren's own, dated three days after her death. Beat: inheritance reframed as obligation.

chapters.title: Dev Comes Early
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Worried by Petra's flat voice on the phone, Dev drives up unannounced and finds the house warm when it should be freezing, and Petra talking in their sleep. Beat: love arriving where it isn't safe, tenderness laced with alarm.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra plays back the sleep recorder out of scientific habit and hears themselves ask questions they don't remember asking — and a second voice answering, low and patient, calling them 'the last note.' Beat: denial collapses; the horror becomes intimate.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra interrogates the recording all night, transcribing. The voice knows the hospice, knows Mrs. Adeyemi's counting, knows Petra's childhood. It asks one question back: 'Will you finish it?' Beat: the entity as conversationalist — worse than any monster.

chapters.title: The Choir Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs: Dev hears harmonies through the floorboards; neighbor Ilsa Brandt, ninety and sharp, confirms she heard them as a girl. Beat: the haunting widens beyond Petra, becoming communal history.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Over tea and brandy, Ilsa describes the founding families, the winter of 1893, and the children who went into the cellar singing so the town could keep its harvest. She warns: 'It doesn't take the unwilling. That's the cruelty of it.' Beat: exposition delivered as grief.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Fragmented
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The ledger's final pages hold half a rite — verses torn out, instructions in Maren's hand ending mid-sentence. The frost on the cellar door now forms legible notation. Beat: the shape of the task appears, incomplete and ominous.

chapters.title: First Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weather report: hard frost in eleven days. The voice in the recordings grows warmer, more helpful, offering to 'help you finish.' Petra catches themselves answering aloud. Beat: seduction begins; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: The Hospice Calls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A dying patient, Mr. Okafor, counts backwards and then — for the first time — says Petra's name at zero. Petra realizes the counting was never random; it was roll call. Beat: the two worlds (hospice and house) fuse.

chapters.title: Dev Sees the Pattern
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, a data analyst, maps the ledger: every seventh year, a Coldharbour dies at first frost. This is the seventh year. He begs Petra to leave. Beat: love against duty takes its first open form — his plea versus her compulsion.

chapters.title: The Night Petra Answered
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Half-asleep, Petra answers the voice honestly about their loneliness, their disinheritance, their hunger to belong somewhere. The voice promises belonging. Petra wakes at the cellar door, hand on a nail. Beat: self-horror; the enemy is also a mirror.

chapters.title: Maren's Letters
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hidden in the piano bench, letters from Maren to Petra across twelve silent years, never sent — each describing the voice a little more, each begging forgiveness for what the bloodline owes. Beat: the grandmother humanized; grief complicates anger.

chapters.title: The Torn Verses
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa produces the missing ledger pages, kept since 1961 when her sister was 'chosen' and refused. The complete ritual requires a Coldharbour to sing the entity asleep — from inside the cellar. Beat: the cost is named plainly.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra tries the opening verse aloud; the house responds — warmth, light, the sensation of being held. It feels like love. That's how Petra knows it's hunting. Beat: the seduction peaks and turns visible.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Dev arrives again, this time with Ilsa and hospice colleague Ruthie. Against all sense, they refuse to leave Petra alone with the house. Beat: the theme crystallizes — the family Petra chose vs. the lineage that claims them.

chapters.title: What the Voice Offers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The voice negotiates openly now: finish the ritual as written, give it a Coldharbour, and everyone else lives long and well. It shows Petra visions of Dev's happy life without them. Beat: temptation rendered as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie, pragmatic and frightened, suggests burning the house down. The frost patterns on every window rearrange into the same notation overnight. The house objects. Beat: escalation; conventional escape closes off.

chapters.title: The Cellar Opens
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The last brass nail works loose on its own. Below: a stone choir stall facing a wall of black ice, and seven generations of names carved in rings. At the center, a space shaped like a person. Beat: awe and revulsion; the stage is set.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mr. Okafor dies at the hospice, and at the exact moment every window in Coldharbour House frosts solid. The voice says, gently: 'Now there is room.' Beat: midpoint turn — the threat becomes immediate and personal.

chapters.title: Quarantine of One
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev locks the cellar, hides the car keys, and stands guard. Petra loves him for it and resents him for it. The house grows colder around their argument. Beat: love against duty dramatized between the two leads.

chapters.title: The Voice Wears Faces
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The recordings now feature Dev's voice, Ruthie's, Ilsa's dead sister's — the entity has learned them all. Petra can no longer trust which loved ones are real. Beat: paranoia fractures the found family's trust.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa admits she let her sister go down alone in 1961 because she was afraid, and has paid for sixty years of silence. She gives Petra the final instruction Maren entrusted to her. Beat: guilt transmuted into gift; the elder passes the burden knowingly.

chapters.title: The Verse Nobody Sang
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Studying the complete rite, Petra notices a gap: the founders' version ends with surrender, but Maren's marginalia sketches an alternative — a name given, not a body. Unfinished. Untested. Beat: hope enters through scholarship.

chapters.title: Frost Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The forecast hardens: tomorrow night, the season's first killing frost. The group shares a last ordinary dinner — laughter that keeps breaking. Beat: calm-before-the-sacrifice, tender and doomed-feeling.

chapters.title: The House Makes Its Argument
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Overnight, the house shows Petra every kindness: warm rooms, Maren's presence, the smell of childhood. It argues that duty and love are the same thing here. Petra nearly believes it. Beat: the antagonist's strongest case.

chapters.title: Dev's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev secretly offers himself to the voice in exchange for Petra — and is refused. 'Not your note to sing.' He returns shaken, having learned the entity wants Petra specifically, by blood and by loneliness. Beat: love tested and found insufficient to substitute.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Frost begins forming the final pattern on the cellar glass. With hours left, Petra descends voluntarily, taking the ledger, the verses, and a decision not yet spoken aloud. The others follow anyway. Beat: descent — literal and moral.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. In the cellar, the black ice shows faces: every Coldharbour who ever sang. The entity speaks through all of them at once, and its true voice underneath is small, old, and terribly lonely. Beat: the monster gains a face and a wound.

chapters.title: The Old Rite Fails
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra attempts the founders' ritual as written and it rejects them — the ice demands willingness without reservation, and Petra's love for the living contaminates the offering. The frost pattern nears completion. Beat: climax part one — the inherited answer breaks.

chapters.title: A Name, Freely Given
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra abandons the founders' text and sings Maren's unfinished alternative: giving the entity not their body but their name — Coldharbour, the last of the line — as an act of chosen kinship rather than sacrifice. The ice drinks the name. Beat: climax part two — love against duty resolved by fusing them.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The frost pattern stops one line short of completion. The cellar goes still and warm. Petra emerges gray-lipped, alive, and unable to say their own surname — the word now lives in the wall. Beat: victory with a price tag.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Winter
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Days later: the house is just a house. Ilsa weeps over her sister's memory finally at rest. But at the hospice, a dying patient counts backwards and, at zero, whispers 'thank you' — and Petra hears it answered. Beat: resolution tinged with ambiguity.

chapters.title: What Petra Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra remains at Coldharbour House, nursing again in the village, Dev splitting his weeks between. Sometimes Petra hums and the floorboards hum back, companionably. Beat: found family and haunted inheritance reconciled into a new normal.

chapters.title: The Eighth Year
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. One year on, first frost again. The recordings capture a second voice once more — but now it only asks one question: 'Are you staying?' And Petra answers, 'Yes.' Beat: the relationship with the dark transformed from predation to covenant.

chapters.title: Coda: Sheet Music for Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing. Petra adds a final entry to the ledger — their own name written not as a debt but as a signature — and leaves the book open on the piano for whoever inherits next. The last image: frost blooming on the glass in shapes like applause. Beat: peace earned, mystery preserved.
